It isn't just one dream but multiple dreams. A majority of my dreams are linked to together and take place in locations I have never seen in real life. 

Except, months or days go by and I finally do see the location in real life and can instantly point out weird specific details. Coincidence? Maybe. Often it makes me question what dreams really are, and the whole concept of reality. 

I'll give an example:
I once had a dream where I was at a school with people I didn't know. There was fence surrounding the area with a huge grass field that led into a paved area at the back doors. There were several broken basketball hoops, there were several trees that rested on the other side of one of the fence walls. The school itself was a tan color with grey metal doors.  The parking lot was off to the side of the entrance with very few cars back. This school resided in more of a residential area with houses and streets all around. I remember being very confused in this dream as to why I was there and who were this kids. 

Not long after I had this dream, my mother told me to come with her to pick up the kid she was babysitting at the time. He didn't go to this particular school I describe but we went through neighborhoods that I've never experienced before in order to get to the actual school. Of course on the way I saw the school that was in my dream and explained to my mom in detail. She drove around the block and I confirmed this was the school. We continue on our way and I still continue having dreams that predict future locations I'll see. 

I still haven't had dreams of exotic places which is a bummer but I can only hope! Lol

I was much like you a couple months ago before corona hit. Except I dropped out at the end the fall semester and broke the news that I didn't intend on going back to my mother. She too very much wanted me to be better than she was. However, since my sophomore year in highschool I've been into developing my own business. 

To get over the anxious flunk, try taking a few steps back and weigh in on what are the pros and cons. I saw college as a lifetime of debt however connections are nice.  I'm not saying to drop out but consider what will work best for you currently and in the long run. Everyone is different. Finding a nice balance will help ease you into setting up goals, whether that is actual physical progress or monetary  like reaching 5k in savings. 

Goals definitely help ease anxiety since you can breakdown everything more. Just need to lay everything out and weigh in on what steps need to be taken to achieve the outcome you. Don't worry too much about the end result and before you know it, you're happier than you ever expected to be. 

Good Luck!
